records.reason: The potion grants a temporary offensive action whose entire content is area damage and a basic save for OTHER creatures; nothing about the drinker's own statistics changes.
Same as the lesser potion — the granted Energy Breath action only deals damage to creatures in an area; no owner-facing standing change.

Relic aspect activation that casts enthrall on other creatures; its rank is 'half the relic's level' so no fixed innateSpells rank exists, and the legendary-proficiency clause only removes the TARGETS' critical success.
A room-sized artifact installation resolved entirely by the GM (secret DC 30 checks, essence streams, paralysing anyone who stands in them); it confers nothing on a character sheet.

Thrown activation that deals the Frozen Lava effect to creatures in the area; the 2d4-hour self-reforming only means the item comes back to your pack, which is inventory bookkeeping, not a sheet change.
Same chassis as eternal-eruption — target-side area damage on activation; the reforming is item bookkeeping.

While invested and worn the ring is a permanent SENSE for the owner — 'you can see clearly into the Ethereal Plane with a range of 60 feet' — but the record carries no senses/passiveEffects at all, so an owner's senses line never changes. (Being visible to ethereal creatures in return is the GM's side.)
A permanent light source (bright light 20 ft, dim 20 more). Illumination is environmental and adjudicated at the table; no character statistic moves.
Shows the paths its investor has travelled — pure information the GM narrates; the Trick Magic Item check to read another creature's paths is a standard action against a stated DC.
Ammunition whose whole effect is an explosion dealing damage to creatures in the area with a save; nothing accrues to the shooter.
Same as explosive-ammunition — area damage to creatures on a hit, no owner-side change.

A talisman that, for 1 minute, makes the affixed weapon count as adamantine/cold iron/dawnsilver. Precious material matters only for overcoming a specific target's resistances, which is adjudicated per target; it changes no number on the owner's sheet.
Same as the high-grade orb — a temporary material swap that only matters against a target's resistances, resolved at the table.
Mundane clockwork tool: permission to Interact with an object up to 10 feet away. No bonus, no standing change.
Mundane gear that works 'as if it were a length of rope' — an anchor and a 20-foot descent, resolved with normal Athletics/Interact rules.
Reprint of the extendable pincer — a mundane tool granting permission to pick up an object at range; no mechanical field applies.

Registered in core.runes as a weapon property rune ('extending', slot weapon, kind property), so it can be etched and shows on the weapon; its activation (reach 60 ft for one Strike) is resolved and gone in the same moment.
Registered in core.runes as 'extending-greater' (slot weapon, kind property); the reach-120-ft Strike is a one-moment activation with no standing change.
Ammunition that removes persistent acid/fire damage from the creature you hit and lowers THAT creature's flat-check DC; every effect lands on the target.

Supplies 5 rounds of breathable air handled by the ordinary hold-your-breath rules, and its reaction is an immediate re-save against an inhaled affliction — both resolved at the table with no standing modifier.
Crafting/downtime device that converts objects into raw materials worth a fraction of their Price; it is a wealth/GM adjudication, not a character statistic.

The 'see through the patch' line is flavour, and the activation is a one-moment fortune effect: roll the concealed/hidden flat check twice. Flat checks are not one of the stat lanes and nothing persists.

While worn and invested the pendant is an always-on warning for the OWNER — 'when a hostile creature comes within 30 feet of you, the stone glows with moonlight only you can see' — yet the record carries no senses/passiveEffects, so the sheet never shows this standing detection. (The once-per-hour blinding burst is target-side and needs nothing.)
On a hit the bullet casts revealing light centred on the target's space; the entire effect (and its DC 23 save) belongs to the creatures caught in the burst.
Mundane smuggling container with a stated Perception DC to find the compartment — a GM-side search DC, not an owner statistic.

An inhaled poison with a save DC and stages; if a character suffers it the resulting dazzled/sickened/confused conditions are applied through the normal condition tracker, and using it on others is target-side.
A prop restraint: a hidden release the wearer can trigger with one Interact, and an observer's check to spot it. Both sides are table adjudication with no standing change.
A hired NPC service (a paid alibi), priced by level; entirely downtime/GM narrative with no mechanical field of any kind.
Hired-NPC alibi service — downtime/GM adjudication only, no owner-facing mechanics.

Hired-NPC alibi service — downtime/GM adjudication only, no owner-facing mechanics.
A container whose stats (Hardness 4, HP 16, BT 8) protect the creature inside; line-of-effect and the 2-action enter/exit are table adjudication, and nothing modifies the owner.
Storage logistics for a familiar — it melds into your skin with its own single action. The familiar's own abilities are unchanged and the owner gains no statistic.

The activation turns the fan into a real wooden buckler (Hardness 3, HP 6, BT 3) and back, but the record is plain 'equipment' with no shield statistics and no toggle, so an owner can never wield it as a shield or Raise it. The unfurled state persists until you collapse it again, which is exactly an item mode.

mode.name: Fan Buckler (Unfurled)
mode.note: Unfurled: the fan is a wooden buckler (Hardness 3, HP 6, BT 3). Raise it for the buckler's +1 circumstance AC; one Interact collapses it back into a fan.

records.reason: Registered in core.runes as the 'fanged' weapon property rune, so it can be etched onto a melee weapon; the polymorph into an animal that wields it in its jaws is a form change resolved at the table.
Attunes up to three sets of mundane clothing and swaps them onto you on command — wardrobe logistics with no bonus, and expressly not armour.

On a hit you make one roll that either fixes this Strike's damage dice at average+1 or splits the damage back onto you; it is resolved inside the single attack, and the resulting HP change goes through the normal damage tracker.
Registered in core.runes as the 'fearsome' weapon property rune (slot weapon, kind property); its effect — the TARGET becomes frightened 1 on a critical hit — lands on the creature you hit.
Registered in core.runes as 'fearsome-greater' (slot weapon, kind property); frightened 2 applies to the target of the critical hit, not the owner.
Creates a bush that provides standard cover and berries worth 1 HP each when eaten — battlefield terrain plus HP handled by the damage/healing tracker; nothing standing accrues to the owner.
Turns permanently into a 20-foot wooden ladder — it creates an object, which is table geography, not a character statistic.
Creates a swan boat with its own carrying capacity and Speed for a day; a vehicle/terrain effect the GM runs, with no owner-facing change.
Grows a 60-foot oak on an unoccupied patch of soil — an object created in the environment, resolved at the table.
A pet that explicitly cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way; it carries no statistics to deliver.

Relic aspect whose benefit is defined by the relic's current emotional state elsewhere ('the emotional fervor benefits for your relic's emotional state'); this record names no bonus of its own, so there is nothing concrete to grant.

This item record has an empty description — the real Fetching Bangles content lives in the ikon record of the same name, whose Immanence aura acts on other creatures. There is no rules text here to model.
Restraints applied to a prisoner: the -20-foot Speed penalty and the manipulate-disruption hit the BOUND creature, and the escape DCs are Thievery checks against the item.
Same as the other fetters — every effect (Speed penalty, manipulate disruption, escape DC) applies to the creature bound in them, not the owner.
Same as the other fetters — the penalties belong to the restrained creature; the owner gains nothing.
Same as the other fetters — the penalties belong to the restrained creature; the owner gains nothing.

A starting shopping bundle (scale mail, dagger, grappling hook, adventurer's pack, plus a weapon option). It confers no rules effect of its own — the contents are ordinary items bought individually, and each already carries its own statistics.

Printed as a '+1 trident', but the record carries only the base weapon statistics (1d8 piercing, spear group, thrown 20) — potency lives on the inventory instance's runes, which this item never sets, so a buyer silently wields a plain trident. Flag it so the owner knows the +1 is part of the item. (The Fluid Length activation only swaps reach/thrown, which no item field expresses, and is table-resolved.)

situational.when: Fighter's Fork is a +1 trident — etch potency 1 on it

records.reason: An artifact execution device: it decapitates a restrained creature and traps its soul. Everything happens to the victim and to the GM's cosmology; the wielder gains no statistic.
